## Review Summary

This PR reconciles documentation and prompt files with the actual state of the Python-native orchestrator implementation. It updates ADR references (ADR 001 → ADR 007/008), annotates inactive pipeline phases with "not yet implemented" notes, marks the PRD status as "Implemented — partial", and corrects the README's architecture description and wiki update frequency. The changes are documentation-only and well-scoped. Two warnings identify stale references that this PR missed: the README project structure tree still says "Use cases and services" and the PRD Goal 5 still references the retired `src/application/services/` layer.

**Files Reviewed:** 4
**Findings:** 0 Critical, 2 Warning, 3 Suggestion

---

## Findings

### Warning Findings

#### [W-01] README project structure tree still says "Use cases and services"

```
Category: Documentation
Severity: Warning
File: README.md
Lines: 157
Description: The Architecture section (line 27) was correctly updated from "Use cases and services" to "Use cases and strategies", but the deeper 📁 Project Structure tree (line 157) still reads `├── application/             # Use cases and services`. This is the exact inconsistency that the PR set out to fix — the services layer was retired per ADR 008 and the PR's own Architecture section update acknowledges this. A reader scanning the project structure tree will see the stale label.
Suggestion: Change line 157 from `│   ├── application/             # Use cases and services` to `│   ├── application/             # Use cases and strategies` to match the Architecture section update.
```

#### [W-02] PRD Goal 5 still references retired `src/application/services/`

```
Category: Documentation
Severity: Warning
File: docs/planning/python-native-migration/prd.md
Lines: 24
Description: Goal 5 states: "Build a Python orchestrator that executes the story generation pipeline phases sequentially, calling `src/application/services/` directly in-process." This directly contradicts the Superseded Decisions section added by this same PR, which explains that ADR 008 retired the services layer and the orchestrator now calls `src/tools/` directly. The Non-Goals section was updated, the Tool Execution section was updated, and the architecture diagram was annotated — but Goal 5 was left unchanged. A reader encountering Goal 5 before the Superseded Decisions section will see an uncorrected statement of intent that was never implemented.
Suggestion: Update Goal 5 to read: "Build a Python orchestrator that executes the story generation pipeline phases sequentially, calling `src/tools/` directly and loading agent prompts from `prompts/agents/`." Add a parenthetical note: "(Originally planned to call `src/application/services/`; superseded by ADR 008 — see Superseded Decisions.)"
```

### Suggestions

#### [S-01] SKILL.md per-chapter diagram labels "Chapter Savepoint (7g)" — should be "Handoff (7g)"

```
Category: Documentation
Severity: Suggestion
File: prompts/skills/story-pipeline/SKILL.md
Lines: 51
Description: The per-chapter loop diagram's rightmost box reads "Chapter Savepoint (7g)". Per the Phase 7 sub-phase table (lines 151–162), 7g is "Handoff artifact" and 7h is the savepoint. The label "Chapter Savepoint" describes 7h, not 7g. This is a pre-existing issue (present on development before this PR), but this PR adds the ⏳ marker to 7f and 7.5 in the same diagram without correcting the 7g label, making it a good opportunity to fix it.
Suggestion: Change the diagram box from `│ Chapter Savepoint  │` / `│ (7g)               │` to `│ Handoff Artifact   │` / `│ (7g) ⏳            │` to match the sub-phase table. If 7h (the actual savepoint step) should appear in the diagram, add it as a separate box.
```

#### [S-02] story-orchestrator.md per-chapter table row 6 labels 7g as "not yet wired" but 7g is also described in detail in the same file

```
Category: Documentation
Severity: Suggestion
File: prompts/agents/story-orchestrator.md
Lines: 207
Description: The Per-Chapter Required Sequence table marks 7g as "not yet wired in active orchestrator", which is accurate. However, the detailed Phase 7g section (lines 289–312) provides full dispatch instructions without any "not yet implemented" annotation at the section level (unlike Phases 6, 7a, 7d, 7f, and 7.5 which all have blockquote annotations). The table note is the only indicator. Adding a consistent blockquote annotation at the top of the 7g section would match the pattern used for other inactive phases.
Suggestion: Add a `> **Not yet implemented in active orchestrator.** Handoff artifact generation is defined in this spec but not wired in the chapter loop.` blockquote at the top of the `#### 7g. Generate Chapter Handoff Artifact` section, matching the pattern used for Phases 6, 7a, 7d, 7f, and 7.5.
```

#### [S-03] PRD Goal 2 references `src/application/` broadly without noting the services retirement

```
Category: Documentation
Severity: Suggestion
File: docs/planning/python-native-migration/prd.md
Lines: 22
Description: Goal 2 says "Preserve all existing domain logic (`src/domain/`, `src/application/`, `src/infrastructure/`) without rewrites." While technically true (the strategies sub-package under `src/application/` was preserved), the bare `src/application/` reference is ambiguous now that the services sub-package was retired. A reader could interpret this as including `src/application/services/`.
Suggestion: Change to `src/application/strategies/` or add a parenthetical: `(strategies only; services/ retired per ADR 008)`.
```

---

## Overall Assessment

The PR is documentation-only and correctly addresses the core reconciliation goal: updating ADR references, annotating inactive pipeline phases, and correcting the README architecture description and wiki update frequency. The changes are consistent across the four files and the annotation pattern (blockquote + table notes + ⏳ markers) is applied uniformly. The two warnings identify references to the retired services layer that this PR missed in the same files it was editing — the README project structure tree and the PRD Goals section. These are straightforward fixes that would complete the reconciliation. No correctness, security, or test coverage concerns apply since no production code was changed. The PR is ready for merge after addressing W-01 and W-02.
